steps: Permit & location
Consult the authority having jurisdiction about a permit before installing. The BX24 is not approved for mobile homes.

Consult the authority having jurisdiction (municipal building department, fire department, etc.) to see whether a permit is needed. The Boxer BX24 is not approved for mobile home installation.

  • Do not install in a sleeping room (certification label, p. 4).
  • Canada: do not install in an alcove. USA: adhere to the minimum clearances (p. 13).
  • Certified for insulated, habitable rooms. It is not designed for a concrete, uninsulated basement or a shop/garage, where a constant call for heat over-fires it; damage from that voids the warranty (p. 14).
Fit the base kit
The stove must be installed with Blaze King Leg Kit Z2133 or Pedestal Kit Z2126, attached as instructed. The pedestal cavity is certified for wood storage.
Set clearances
Position the stove to the roof-exit or wall-exit clearance table and its lettered drawing on p. 8. Clearances may only be reduced by means the regulatory authority approves.
Floor protection
On a combustible floor, use a non-combustible floor shield: in the USA, 16" in front of and 8" either side of the loading door, plus a shield under the chimney connector extending 2" each side.
Combustion air
In airtight homes, balance intake air against HRVs, air handlers, range hoods, dryers and other exhausting appliances. A fresh air intake into the stove's room is recommended.
Flue pipe
Run 6" 24 MSG steel flue pipe as directly as possible and only within the room; fasten every joint with sheet metal screws. Never pass it through an attic, closet, floor or ceiling.

• Flue pipe: 6" diameter, 24 MSG steel; no aluminum or galvanized steel (p. 8).
  • A chimney connector is required: don't install the chimney directly at the stove outlet.
  • Double wall pipe from stove top adaptor to ceiling support box is recommended. For a wall exit, 3 ft of vertical from stove top to elbow; use a pair of 45 degree elbows rather than one 90 (p. 9).
  • Use a chimney support package through a ceiling to a listed prefab chimney, and a listed wall thimble through a combustible wall.
  • Keep an effective vapor barrier where the chimney or vent passes through the exterior.
Chimney
Connect to a listed UL 103HT chimney or a code-compliant masonry chimney that serves no other appliance. It must be at least 3ft above the roof penetration and 2ft above anything within 10ft.

• Factory-built: listed, 1" or 2" insulation, suitable for solid fuels (UL 103HT in the USA, CAN/ULC-S629 in Canada). Buy all components from the same prefab chimney manufacturer. An interior chimney is recommended; build a chase around an exterior one.
  • Masonry: have it inspected by a certified professional (no cracks, loose mortar, deterioration or blockage) and cleaned first. A stainless steel liner, preferably insulated, is recommended (p. 11).
  • Through a combustible wall, use your jurisdiction's approved methods (NFPA in the USA, CAN/CSA-B365 in Canada).
  • Connecting to a chimney that serves another appliance voids the warranty.
Chimney height
Blaze King recommends at least 15 ft from stove top to termination at 0 - 1000 ft elevation, more at altitude and with elbows, a "T" or horizontal run. No more than one offset (two elbows).

Minimum recommended chimney height, stove top to termination, by elevation and number of elbows (0 / 2 X 15° / 2 X 30° / 2 X 45°):

0 - 1000 ft15 / 16 / 18 / 19 ft
1000 - 2000 ft15.5 / 16.5 / 18.5 / 19.5 ft
2000 - 3000 ft16 / 17 / 19 / 20 ft
3000 - 4000 ft16.5 / 17.5 / 19.5 / 20.5 ft
4000 - 5000 ft17 / 18 / 20 / 21 ft
5000 - 6000 ft17.5 / 18.5 / 20.5 / 21.5 ft
6000-7000 ft18 / 19 / 21 / 22 ft
7000 - 8000 ft18.5 / 19.5 / 21.5 / 22.5 ft

No more than one offset (two elbows) is allowed; two 45° elbows equal one 90° elbow. Add vertical height for other components: 90° elbow = 2.0 ft, "T" section = 3.0 ft, 1.0 ft of horizontal run = 2 ft of vertical rise.

Manual example at sea level: 15.0 ft minimum + one 90° elbow 2.0 ft + 2.0' horizontal run 4.0 ft + one base "T" 3.0 ft = 24.0 ft. The figures are guidelines; draft still depends on the site (see "Draft performance", p. 9).
Fan kit power
Plug the fan kit's three-prong grounded plug directly into a properly grounded three-hole receptacle. Never cut the grounding prong or route the cord in front of or under the stove.
Installer notes & handover
Complete the installer page at the back (dealer, installer, date installed, appliance serial no.) and leave the manual with the homeowner.

Thermostat set too high → lower the setting
Loading door gasket leaking → replace gasket and/or adjust the door

Wood too small → use larger pieces

Chimney too cold → use double wall stove pipe
Not enough vertical rise → minimum 36" before elbows; two 45s instead of a 90

Improper operation → check thermostat setting and operating procedure
Obstruction in chimney or cap → clean chimney, remove obstructions

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Check that all the firebricks are in place and build the fire right on the bottom bricks, with no grate. Don't leave the stove unattended while it gets going.

  1. Turn the thermostat to High and the fan (if you have one) off.
  2. Open the loading door and the bypass door.
  3. Put 10 balls of non-glossy paper toward the front of the firebox. Crisscross 20 pieces of kindling on top, leaving air gaps.
  4. Light it and leave the loading door cracked open for about 3 to 5 minutes.
  5. When the kindling is fully on fire, add two or three medium logs. Keep the door unlatched for about 5 minutes while they catch.
  6. Latch the loading door but leave the bypass open; an open loading door now can make the combustor fail early.
  7. When nearly all the wood is burning, fill the stove, laying wood as far back as you can. Latch the door. Once the thermometer needle is in the Active zone, close the bypass door.
  8. Leave it on High for 20-30 minutes, then turn the thermostat down gradually. Turn the fan on after this warm-up.

Turned down too low, too fast, the fire may go out or the needle may fall to Inactive. Turn it back up and let the fire re-establish.

First fires: the curing paint gives off a strong smell and smoke. Burn at a low setting for several hours with a door or window open. Any color change evens out after a few fires.

reload.title: Reloading the stove
reload.html:
Check the thermometer first. If the needle is still in the Active zone, use these steps. If it has dropped to Inactive, start over with the lighting steps.

  1. Have the next load ready. Turn the thermostat to High and wait 2 minutes.
  2. To cut down on smoke in the room, you can open the bypass door and wait another 2 minutes.
  3. Crack the loading door open and give it about a minute to settle.
  4. Open the door slowly and load. If a lot of smoke spills out, close the door partway until the chimney draws again.
  5. Latch the door and close the bypass door right away (if you opened it). Leave it on High for 20 to 30 minutes, then turn it down.

On low settings you may see little flame. That's fine: the needle stays in the Active zone while the burn continues.

Deposits on the glass? Long, very low burns leave creosote on the glass. Run on High for about 30 minutes to burn most of it off.
Load only the shaded area shown in the manual's loading diagram (p. 17). Loading wood anywhere else voids the warranty and is a safety hazard.

controls.title: Thermostat, bypass door & thermometer
controls.html:
Thermostat knob

The knob is on the left side. High gives the fastest burn and the most heat; turn it counter clockwise for less. Make changes gradually, since a fast change can make the thermostat work poorly. It is set at the factory, so don't tamper with it.

Bypass door

The bypass door, inside the top of the firebox, lets exhaust skip the combustor for a while. You open it when lighting, and if you like when reloading. With the bypass handle, hook the side of the latch and pull out to open; press the center and push in to close. Never touch the latch itself: it can burn you badly.

Catalytic thermometer

The dial on top shows whether the combustor is working. Keep the needle in the Active zone. Inactive means it is below 500F and not burning clean. Turn the fan off before you read it.

Note: p. 16 says to turn the fan off for about 5 minutes before reading the thermometer; p. 27 and p. 34 say 10 minutes.

Fan (optional kit)

Keep it off until the stove is up to temperature. About 30 minutes after the fire is established, match fan speed to the thermostat: low with low, high with high.

wood.title: Choosing and checking your wood
wood.html:
Burn natural cord wood only. Wet wood wastes heat drying itself out and greatly increases creosote.

  • Use only seasoned wood at 20% moisture or lower: split and stack it so air reaches all of it, and keep it out of rain and snow for at least 24 months.
  • Hardwood and softwood both burn well; denser hardwood burns a little slower and longer.
  • Go easy on lumber offcuts, very dry small pieces and pressed logs. Used in excess, they can overheat and permanently damage the firebox.

Check it with a moisture meter

  1. Pick three logs at random and split each one down the middle.
  2. On each split face, take readings 2" from either end and in the middle, pins in line with the grain.
  3. Average all the readings for an approximate figure.
Never burn salt-water driftwood (it also voids the warranty), treated wood, coal, charcoal, colored paper, cardboard, solvents or garbage. Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene or charcoal lighter fluid to start or freshen a fire. Never burn wet or unseasoned wood: it can build up excess creosote, and if that ignites it can cause a chimney fire that may lead to a house fire and serious injury. Burning wood that isn't seasoned may also damage the combustor, and it will void all warranties (p. 21).

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
The best way to keep the glass clean is to run the stove on a high burn for a while after each reload. Much of the deposit comes from moisture driven out of fresh wood. Leaving the thermostat higher for 30 minutes to an hour before turning it low for an overnight burn also helps.

Cleaning by hand

  • Clean only when the stove and glass are cool. Never clean hot glass.
  • Use a soft cloth and no abrasive cleaners.
  • After any cleaner, rinse the glass well with water. Leftover cleaner bakes on and can be very hard to remove.
Be gentle with it. Don't strike the glass or slam the door, and don't use the stove if the glass or its gasket is broken. The warranty covers thermal breakage only. Replace it only with 5 mm ceramic glass.

ash.title: Emptying the ashes
ash.html:
Take ashes out whenever they come within one inch of the door opening. Don't remove them all: wood burns best on a bed of ashes about 1/2" thick.

  1. Make sure the fire is out and the stove is cool to the touch.
  2. Put the ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Don't put other waste in it.
  3. Set the closed container on a noncombustible floor or on the ground outside, well away from anything that can burn.
  4. If you will bury or scatter the ashes, keep them in the closed container until every cinder has cooled.
Never store hot ashes in a garage or basement. They give off carbon monoxide and flammable gases that can cause suffocation and death.

After the last fire of the season, remove all the ash from the firebox.

chimney.title: Creosote and chimney fires
chimney.html:
When wood burns slowly, tar and vapors condense in the cooler chimney as creosote. If it ignites, it makes an extremely hot fire. Hotter fires leave less creosote.

  • Inspect the flue pipe and chimney regularly through the heating season until you know how often they need cleaning.
  • Have the chimney and the stove cleaned at least once a year, or as often as needed. A professional chimney sweep is recommended.
  • Open the bypass door before the chimney is swept so soot and creosote fall into the firebox.

If a chimney fire starts

  1. Turn the thermostat knob fully counter clockwise and make sure the loading door and bypass door are closed.
  2. Call the fire department.
  3. Check the chimney, attic and roof for anything hot enough to catch fire. If needed, use a fire extinguisher or a garden hose.
  4. Don't use the stove again until you are certain the chimney isn't damaged.
Chimney fire damage is not covered by the warranty. Make sure everyone at home knows the plan.

combustor.title: Looking after the catalytic combustor
combustor.html:
The combustor sits in the dome at the top of the firebox, behind the flame shield. If it isn't working properly, you lose heating efficiency and get more emissions and creosote.

Check it

  • Look it over at least three times each heating season for physical wear. Don't remove it unless performance has dropped.
  • A healthy combustor keeps the thermometer above 500 F (Active) and often passes 1000 F.
  • Smoke check: open the bypass door for a few minutes and watch the chimney, then close it. There should be much less smoke with the bypass closed.

Needle stuck in Inactive?

Burn a well-established fire for 1 hour, turn to medium-low, and check the needle after 5 minutes. Repeat for at least 3 burn cycles. Still Inactive? With the stove cool, brush the combustor face gently with a soft paint brush or pass a vacuum wand near it, never a hard tool. A hot fire is usually the best cleaner. If it still won't reach Active, stop using the stove and call your dealer (the thermometer itself could also be at fault).

Never run the stove without the combustor installed. Doing so leads to excessive smoke and temperatures that could cause a house fire and serious injury (p. 21).

safety.title: Safety around the stove
safety.html:
• Have at least one smoke detector and one carbon monoxide monitor in the room with the stove, plus more around the house. Don't disable or move them.
  • If an alarm sounds, get everyone out. Fix the cause only once there is no risk.
  • Keep at least one fire extinguisher in a central spot everyone knows.
  • The stove is hot when it's running. Keep children and pets from touching it.
  • Keep furniture, clothing and other combustibles at least 48" from the front. Don't store wood in the clearances or the space you need for reloading and ash removal.
  • Run it with the door closed; open it only to add wood. Don't block the combustion air openings.
  • Don't run it if the door gasket is missing or damaged. To check the seal with the stove cool, latch the door on a dollar bill and pull it out: no resistance means the door needs adjusting. Repeat all the way around.
Not a trash burner. Garbage, treated wood and flammable fluids can release toxic fumes and carbon monoxide, or over-fire the stove.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Blaze King's limited warranty starts on the original owner's purchase date, for stoves bought from an authorized dealer and installed in the USA or Canada.

Catalytic combustor6 years
Stove body & steel firebox parts5 years
Fans, modular thermostat, door handle steel parts2 years
All parts & materials, incl. exterior paint1 year

Combustor: no charge for the first 3 years, then you pay 60%, 70% and 80% of the current retail price in years 4, 5 and 6. For other parts covered past the first year, you pay 20% in year 2, 40% in year 3, 60% in year 4 and 80% in year 5.

  • Report a problem to your dealer within 30 days of finding it, with proof of purchase.
  • Not covered: gasket material, firebrick, over-firing, salt-saturated or treated wood, and chimney fire damage.
  • Original purchaser only; it can't be transferred.
This is a summary. The full conditions, exclusions and limitations are in the manual.

specChimney.title: Chimney
specChimney.html:
Connect to a chimney meeting the UL 103 requirements for Type HT chimneys, or a code-approved masonry chimney with a flue liner. Don't connect to a chimney serving another appliance, or to air distribution ductwork.

Min. vertical height, 0 - 1000 ft elev.15 ft, stove top to termination

Above the roof penetration3ft (p. 10)

Use a pair of 45 degree elbows rather than a single 90. Build a chase around an outside chimney where possible to keep it warm. Taller chimneys are recommended at higher elevations and with elbows: see the "Chimney height" step (p. 12).

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Wall, corner and ceiling clearances are given as lettered dimensions for roof-exit and wall-exit installations, parallel or corner. The text doesn't say which letter is which, so they aren't repeated here: use the drawing on p. 8 (the same table is on the certification label, p. 4).

Single wall pipe (Canada)18" minimum
Combustible objects, front48" minimum (p. 19)
  • Clearances may only be reduced by means approved by the regulatory authority.
  • Pipe clearances: check local codes and the pipe manufacturer.
  • Canada: do not install in an alcove. USA: adhere to the minimum clearances (p. 13).
  • Don't store wood within the clearances; the pedestal base cavity (S.Z2126) is certified for wood storage.
Wall exit B is 14" (356 mm) and D is 19.125" (483 mm), as on the label (p. 4); the p. 8 table prints the same inch values with 365 mm and 385 mm. G is 5.75" (146 mm) in the USA on p. 8; the label prints 5 3/4" (147 mm).

specFloor.html:
No thermal hearth pad is required, but on a combustible floor a non-combustible floor shield must be used.

Note: the Canadian door-side figure is printed with two metric values: p. 8 gives ember protection on a side with a door as 18" (450 mm); the label (p. 4) gives 18" (456 mm) in front of the loading door.

Canada (CSA B365): the 18" on a door side runs the full width of the stove plus the 8" on each side; within 8" of a wall the ember pad need only reach the wall. Don't lay an ember pad on carpet unless it is supported against shifting. Adhesive vinyl flooring in front of the stove isn't recommended. The label (p. 4) gives the minimum sizes as width x depth.

Note: the label (p. 4) says the floor protector may be any non-combustible material or a listed floor protector; p. 8 says the shield must be listed under UL 1618-2009 (Type 1).

review.notes: Single combined installation & operation manual (180-BX24 v2.51, Feb 14, 2025); physical page numbers equal the printed ones. Not in the manual, so left out: an efficiency figure (catalog 78.7% HHV; the manual only names the B415.1-10 method and HHV basis), burn time (catalog 25 hr), heating area (catalog 400-1600 sq ft), viewing-glass size (catalog 24" x 11"), fan cfm (catalog 120 cfm; the manual's 120x47 mm is the fan size), and the leg/pedestal kit attachment steps. Figure-only content not transcribed: overall dimensions (p. 7), the lettered clearance and floor-protection dimensions A-L, G1, G2 (pp. 4, 8; the text never defines the letters - the values A 10", B 10"/14", E 2.75", J 49" would match the catalog's brochure clearance note if A=side wall, B=rear wall, E=rear corner, J=ceiling, but that mapping is unconfirmed), the usable loading area (p. 17), bypass latch figures (p. 16), brick layout (p. 37) and the warranty check-mark grid (p. 38; the warranty drawer uses the p. 39-41 text). Text with the 29-code-point font offset was decoded: p. 8 'G2 55.25" (1403 mm) in USA or 57.25" (1454 mm) in Canada' (not used, letter undefined); p. 20 shoulder-season range 'perhaps 55F to 70F (13°C to 21°C)' (not used); p. 36 parts items 3 '2030 Flame shield grate', 7 'Z2022 25 bypass gasket retainer assembly', 9 'Z3030 25 insert thermostat' (not used); p. 37 heading 'Refractory brick layout'. Glyphs 'ϭϬϬΣ' on p. 20 could not be decoded and were ignored. French appears only as the bilingual label text; no smell-gas block applies (wood stove). No error-code table, so codes is empty. The manual repeatedly writes HIGH / ACTIVE / INACTIVE in capitals; owner drawers use High / Active / Inactive.
